intro: A naive slice can put every rare-class example into one split. Allocate indices within each class before evaluating a model.
task: Return deterministic train and test index lists using a separate allocation for each class.
requirements: labels is a nonempty vector of nonnegative integer values. Every observed class has at least two rows. train_fraction is finite and strictly between zero and one.
For a class with n rows, put its first min(n-1, max(1, floor(n*train_fraction))) indices in train and the rest in test.
Return a dictionary with train and test as ascending Python index lists. This deterministic exercise does not shuffle observations.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Collect original indices for each unique label, then compute its clipped training count.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Sort the combined index lists after assigning classes; class order should not reorder the dataset.

explanation: Stratification allocates examples within classes so a small class is not accidentally absent from evaluation. Clipping the allocation leaves at least one row of each observed class on each side.
Split indices before fitting transforms, then fit preprocessing on training rows only. The returned indices preserve original order for transparent inspection.

This deterministic policy is an exercise in allocation, not a universal sampling strategy. If rows are time-ordered or grouped by person, explain why random or stratified row splitting can still produce misleading evaluation.
